narr: A strong upper high over the southeast US and a trough approaching the west coast streamed deep moisture into the Borderland with a low level surface trough located through far west Texas into eastern New Mexico. Slow moving storms brought rainfall amounts of 1 to 3 inches to areas of Dona Ana and Otero counties with the Vado area most significantly impacted.
ev: Significant flash flooding was reported along Interstate 10 which was forced to be closed between Mesquite south through Vado. Video showed turbulent water running over the Frontage Road along I-10 near Vado. Other areas that had significant flooding included High Valley Road near the Vado Quarry, areas in the vicinity of Las Palmeras Road and Jamaica Lane in Berino as well as near Cebolla Lane flooding the nearby neighborhood.

Flash flooding started near Bent with arroyo flooding on Mauer Drive. An arroyo bank was cut with edge of embankment moved 14 feet closer to a home. There was also culvert and road damage along Round Mountain Road. Further west, flash flooding was noted along Tularosa Creek above Bridal Falls. Flooding extended into into a backyard and crawl space of a house with an artificial pond washed out about 4 miles east of Tularosa.
lsr: Video shows deep flooding along High Valley Road near the Vado Quarry and the approach to the Vado Roundabout.
I-10 is closed due to flooding at MM 151 and the Vado area; fire crews are unable to get through.
Deep flooding on roads and surrounding homes in vicinity of Las Palmeras Road and Jamaica Lane in Berino. Video posted to social media.
Social media video shows major flash flooding in Vado, with floodwaters from Vado Arroyo breaching an embankment in a settling pond near Cebolla Lane, flooding the neighborhood.
Video shows lingering flooding on I-10 eastbound due to major flooding in the Vado Arroyo, with deep turbulent water running over the Frontage Road.
Road and culvert damage in several places along Round Mountain Road in Bent.
Severe arroyo flooding on Mauer Drive in Bent. Arroyo bank cut, with edge of embankment now 14 feet closer to a home.
Flash flooding along Tularosa Creek above Bridal Falls. Flooding of back yard and into house crawl space, artificial pond washed out. Videos found on social media.
